display.purpose: Every name, title and button label, uppercase; sized by the caller (the phone lobby name shown). Display surfaces size it in --cu: countdown 16, game name 15, play title 8, plaque 6.4 (compact 2.6), announcement 5.5, join heading, notice and open-room button 5.4, game plaque 3.4, roster name 3.2, top tag 2.2.

headline.purpose: Outcome band title on the phone.

plaque.purpose: The four-letter room code on the enamel plaque.

title.purpose: Player name beside their top on the phone.

body.purpose: Running text on the legal page.

label.purpose: Cues, statuses, seat states, band detail, the play header subtitle and tap cue, the roster cue, the back-to-games control and the player count on the game choice.

shadows.name: shadow-phone-control

motion.name: transition-fast
motion.purpose: Press scale, hover fill, knob follow, gauge opacity. Value comes from @adrienlcp/styles tokens.defaults.

motion.name: transition-base
motion.purpose: Stick base re-anchoring, pad fade when inert.

motion.name: transition-slow
motion.purpose: Band wipe (clip-path), seat ground change; multiples drive spins (x2 status ring, x6 won top and rotate cue, x15 lobby top).

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: Default easing for wipes and presses.

motion.name: dash-refill
motion.purpose: Cooldown ring refilling from dashoffset 101 to 0.

motion.name: countdown-beat
motion.value: var(--transition-slow) cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1), from opacity 0 and scale 1.25

motion.name: announcement-wipe

motion.name: top-spin

motion.name: qr-reveal

narrative.overview:
A table game seen from directly above. The display is a billiard-green felt tabletop; every structure on it (arena rim, gutter edge, ticks, rules between zones, tally pips, cooldown gauge) is a brass filet drawn on that felt, never a modelled object. The objects that sit on the table are the furniture of a café: lacquered spinning tops in six seat colours, an enamel-blue plaque for the room code, an ivory QR card, a slate scoreboard framed in walnut. The phone is the same table seen through one seat: its whole ground turns that seat's lacquer and carries the player's own top.

In play, the display's arena is a real-time 3D scene seen through one perspective camera that leans 14° from straight above toward the people standing in front. The table itself stays a plan: unlit felt and brass filets. Before the scene loads, an SVG preview draws the same filets through the same camera (field of view, tilt, framing margin), so the scene lands on it without a jump. Only the tops are modelled: lacquered, clearcoated, ringed in brass, spinning on their point and casting soft ink shadows; a top that loses tips over and sinks into the gutter. The shell around the arena stays neutral: the game hands it a title, a subtitle, a cue, each seat's standing and the announcement of the moment, and the shell draws them in the bistrot vocabulary. For the game choice it hands three more pieces (`GameDefinition`'s `Preview`, `Showcase` and `Cues`): the arena with the demo tops drawn flat on their marks before its scene loads, the game playing by itself, and its pictogram cues.

The display is read from a few metres away by a standing group and is never scrolled, so it is sized on one unit (`--cu`, 1 % of the portrait panel's height, capped by its 9:16 width) and holds a 3 % safe area that never touches the alcove's walls. The phone is used blind under two thumbs, so it carries only the player's top and name, a stick and one button. Density is low on both: few objects, very large uppercase lettering, no explanatory text beyond pictogram cues (the game's two on the join block and the game choice, one tap cue in play).

The bistrot look is fixed whatever the system theme. The home is the game choice and stands on the display like a room: same `--cu` column, same felt. While it is shown, `:root:has(.home-page)` maps the neutral tokens onto the bistrot ones (`ground` felt, `ink` chalk, `ink-muted` soft chalk, `rule` brass at 40 %, `rule-strong` brass-deep, focus brass), so the site footer below the column sits on felt too. Only the legal page and its footer follow light or dark through the neutral `ground` / `ink` tokens. Today the bistrot tokens sit at `:root` and are shared by the room shell (QR, plaque, roster) and the sumo; the product principle is that each game brings its own world while the host stays neutral, so a second game is the moment to split them.
keyCharacteristics: Felt ground, brass filets for every line and ring, no gradients, no glass.
Six lacquered tops, each with a carved glyph, so seats differ by shape as well as colour; flat SVG on every 2D surface, modelled only inside the 3D arena.
The 3D arena is a flat plan with modelled tops on it, framed by a near-vertical camera; every colour it draws comes from the CSS tokens.
Big Shoulders Display Black, uppercase, for everything named; Barlow Semi Condensed for everything read.
Depth from soft ink-tinted shadows and inset double filets, never from blur or glow.
Display sized in `--cu` units inside a 3 % safe area, the game choice included; controller sized in rem and `--pad-unit`.

rules.name: The Filet Rule
rules.body: Structure is drawn, not filled: a ring, a rule, a tick or a gauge is a brass stroke on felt or slate, with opacity carrying its rank. No filled shapes stand in for lines.

rules.name: The Lacquer Rule
rules.body: The six seat lacquers are the only saturated colours, and they appear only as a seat: a top, a phone ground, a named seat. A seat colour never decorates anything that is not a player.

rules.name: The Two Marks Rule
rules.body: A seat is always shown by its top (lacquer plus carved glyph) and its name together, never by colour alone. In the arena, the modelled top carries a name tag hung above it. The game choice's demo tops are nobody's seat, so they go unnamed.

rules.name: The One Source Rule
rules.body: The 3D scene owns no colour. It resolves every token (`--felt`, `--brass`, `--seat`, `--seat-cap`, `--seat-mark`, `--seat-top-ring`, `color-mix` included) through a hidden probe in the page and draws without tone mapping, so the lacquer on the table is the lacquer in the roster.

rules.name: The Two Weights Rule
rules.body: The body face ships 500 and 700 only; anything heavier than regular is written 700, and font synthesis is off.

rules.name: The Names Are Capitals Rule
rules.body: What a player must read from across the room (a name, the code, an outcome) is in the display voice; everything else is a label in the body face.

rules.name: The Ink Shadow Rule
rules.body: Every shadow is soft, offset downward, and tinted with lacquer ink between 30 and 40 %, the 3D scene's shadows included. No hard offsets, no glow, no coloured shadows.

rules.name: The Plan Under Objects Rule
rules.body: In 3D the table stays a plan and only what sits on it is modelled. The rim, gutter, ticks and centre ring are unlit filets at their 2D radii and opacities; depth comes from the tops, their light and their shadows.

dos: **Do** draw every ring, rule, tick and gauge as a brass filet, ranking them by opacity (100 / 70 / 55 / 40 %).
**Do** show a seat with its top and its name together, using `data-seat-slot` to resolve `--seat`, `--seat-cap` and `--seat-mark`.
**Do** set names, codes, titles and button labels in Big Shoulders Display 900 uppercase, and everything else in Barlow Semi Condensed 500 / 700.
**Do** size display surfaces in `--cu` and keep them inside the 3 % safe area.
**Do** tint every shadow with lacquer ink at 30 to 40 %.
**Do** keep the bistrot look fixed regardless of system theme; the game choice stands on the felt too, and only the legal page and its footer follow light / dark.
**Do** let a game speak to the room only through its standings: title, subtitle, cue, pips, fallen and winner marks, and the one announcement band across the header.
**Do** read every 3D colour from the CSS tokens through the probe.
donts: **Don't** paint gradients, glass, blur or glow onto any surface; the table is flat felt, and the only shading is light falling on the modelled lacquer.
**Don't** use a seat lacquer for anything that is not a player.
**Don't** wrap content in generic UI cards; a panel is a table object (slate in walnut, enamel plaque, ivory QR card).
**Don't** add a third weight to the body face or a second weight to the display face.
**Don't** model the arena itself: in the 3D scene the platform, gutter, rim, ticks and centre ring stay unlit felt and brass filets; only the tops are modelled and lit.
**Don't** put shell UI over the arena; news goes in the header band, standings on the roster.
**Don't** hard-code a colour in the renderer.
